sentences.text: Dr.A.K.Jayasankaran Nambiar, J.

When this matter was taken up today, a memo was filed by the Senior Government Pleader,
producing a report furnished by the 3 rd respondent, the SHO, Pulinkunnu Police Station.
A perusal of the said report indicates that on 09.09.2024, when the bail application preferred on behalf of Sri.

Jaimon, who was an L.P. warrantee in L.P. No. 25/2015 of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court,
Ramankary (Crime No. 365/2010 u/s. 420 IPC), came up for orders before the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Ramankary at 12:00 hrs on 09.09.2024, a report was filed on behalf of the SHO,
Pulinkunnu through which the JFCM Court, Ramankary, was apprised of the fact that Sri. Jaimon was also wanted in connection with another warrant that was issued from the JFCM Court,
Kodungalloor.

sentences.text:
It is further stated that a copy of the warrant obtained from the JFCM Court,
Kodungalloor, was also produced before the JFMC Court, Ramankary, WP(C) No.32952/2024 3/7 Order Date : 13-09-2024 :: 2 ::
along with the objection to the bail application, which was considered by the JFMC Court, Ramankary.

Thereafter, when the bail was granted to the said Jaimon by the JFMC Court, Ramankary in connection with Crime No. 365/2010, and Sri. Jaimon had come out of the Court pursuant to the grant of bail, he was arrested in connection with L.P. No.129/2023 in Crime No. 391/2012 u/s. 420 & 34 IPC of Valappad Police Station.
The statement also suggests that there was no altercation between the police officers and the advocates within the premises of JFCM Court, Ramankary.

2. It is the submission of learned Senior Counsel, Gracious Kuriakose, that there was no illegality that was committed by the Police Officers in arresting Sri. Jaimon, within the premises of the JFCM Court, Ramankary, pursuant to the grant of bail to him in another case.

In particular, it is pointed out that the details of the warrant issued in connection with crime registered at Valappad Police Station had already been brought to the notice of the JFCM Court, Ramankary, while it was considering the bail application filed in connection with the case registered by the Pulikunnu Police Station, and that it was not withstanding this aspect being pointed out that the JFCM Court, Ramankary, had granted the bail to Sri. Jaimon.

Learned Senior counsel points out that there was no illegality WP(C) No.32952/2024 4/7 Order Date :
13-09-2024 :: 3 ::
or irregularity in the action taken by the Police in arresting Sri. Jaimon in connection with the warrant issued by the JFCM, Kodungalloor in connection with the crime registered at Valappad Police Station.

3. The submission of Sri. Yashwant Shenoy, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the Kerala High Court Advocate Association on the other hand is that it is difficult to believe that the warrant/arrest issued from the JFCM, Kodungalloor on 09.09.2024 actually reached the JFCM Court, Ramankary by 12 noon the same day and for the said warrant to have been seen by the JFCM Court, Ramankary in the proceedings that took place at 12 noon on the same day.

sentences.text: On a consideration of the submissions made on either side, we prima facie find that the action of the Police officers in arresting Sri. Jaimon in connection with the crime registered at Valappad Police Station, lacked propriety in that the Police officers ought to have found that it was after considering the objection of the prosecution to the grant of bail to Sri. Jaimon in connection with the case registered at Pulinkunnu police station, which objection also included a submission with regard to the existence of another warrant issued by the JFCM Court, Kodungalloor, that bail was granted to Sri. Jaimon by the JFCM, Ramankary.

Under the circumstances,
WP(C) No.32952/2024 5/7 Order Date : 13-09-2024 :: 4 ::
the Police officials ought to have accorded due deference to the order of the JFMC Court, Ramankary, granting bail to Sri. Jaimon and deferred his arrest to a later point in time after a clarification in that regard had been obtained from the JFCM Court, Ramanakary. The position would have been entirely different if the factum of the warrant issued by the JFCM, Kodungalloor against Sri. Jaimon, was not brought to the notice of the JFCM Court, Ramankary, and the said Magistrate had granted the bail only with reference to the crime registered at Pulinkunnu Police Station.

To ignore the bail order granted by the JFCM Court, Ramankary, especially when he had already considered the submission regarding existence of another warrant against Sri. Jaimon in respect of the crime registered at Valappad Police Station, was not an option available to the police officers while carrying out the arrest of Sri. Jaimon, that too within the court premises.

5. We also find force in the submissions of Sri. Yashwant Shenoy that it was virtually impossible for the SHO, Pulinkunnu, to have produced a copy of the warrant issued by the JFCM, Kodungalloor on 09.09.2024, before the JFCM Court, Ramankary at 12 noon the same day.

With a view to obtaining clarity on facts, therefore, we direct the SHO, WP(C) No.32952/2024 6/7 Order Date : 13-09-2024 :: 5 ::
Valappad to file an affidavit before this Court stating the time at which he received the warrant produced herewith as Annexure R2(b) and pertaining to L.P. 129/2023 from the JFCM Court, Kodungalloor, and how he transmitted the same to the SHO,
Pulinkunnu on the same day.
The affidavit of the SHO shall be filed before this Court on 26.09.2024.

Sd/-
Dr. A.K.JAYASANKARAN NAMBIAR JUDGE Sd/-
